correctness.rationale: For n>=10000 and positive powers a=n-tau(n), b=n+1-tau(n+1), an unequal exponent collision sigma(n)^a=sigma(n+1)^b forces both bases to powers of a common C>=2, with exponent s=b/gcd(a,b). The divisor pairing tau(m)<=2sqrt(m) bounds gcd(a,b)<=1+4sqrt(n+1), hence s>sqrt(n+1)/5-1, contradicting s<=log_2(sigma(n))<=log_2(n(1+log n)) by the checked endpoint and derivative comparison. For 2<=n<10000 an independently implemented exact sieve and prime-valuation equality check finds no powered collisions (only n=1 excluded). Therefore every n>=2 collision has equal exponents/bases, i.e. sigma(n)=sigma(n+1), tau(n+1)=tau(n)+1; converse immediate. Parity makes one member square, common odd sigma makes other twice square, yielding x^2-2y^2=+-1 and O(log X) Pell count.
risk: Finite 2<=n<10000 is exhaustive there alone; all larger n rely on analytic growth comparison.
Does not prove conjectured absence of nontrivial collisions.
